item.title: Are these the only portfolio managers doing well during a brutal month for macro?
item.description:
It's been a brutal few weeks for macro hedge fund </news/2021/05/how-to-get-a-job-in-a-global-macro-fund>managers of the world. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/hedge-funds-exiting-crowded-trades-fueled-rout-in-french-bonds>reported last Friday that after losing money in mid-September following the Federal Reserve's first rate increase since 2023, macro funds lost money again last week after carry trades relating to French bonds blew up.
There is blood on the carpet. Some of the best known portfolio managers </news/2023/09/portfolio-manager-job-hedge-fund> at some of the biggest funds are thought to be nursing large losses. None of the funds concerned have confirmed this. Only the unfortunate macro-focused Taula Capital Management </news/diego-megia-taula-capital>is known to have been down 9.4% in September <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-24/hedge-fund-taula-down-9-4-in-volatile-year-for-macro-traders>.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Even Taula, though, is understood to have portfolio managers who are doing well. There are unconfirmed suggestions that Lewis Morton, the former star portfolio manager at Eisler Capital, is up nearly $20m this year and that Josh Blakely, who came from Millennium, is also doing fine.
Similarly, it's suggested that James Watson, </news/now-hedge-fund-balyasny-hired-barclays-head-of-euro-swaps-trading> formerly of Millennium is personally doing well at Balyasny </news/balyasny-hedge-fund> Asset Management, even though Bloomberg said BAM lost money on the French trade. Ex-Goldman Sachs managing director and rates trader Andrew Bound </news/hedge-fund-citadel-london-partners> is said to be up at Citadel. This is unconfirmed by either the individuals or the firms concerned, though.
More broadly, it's thought that many macro teams are nursing large losses that they are unlikely to recover from this year. This is problematic because such portfolio managers become "zombies." </news/millennium-hedge-fund-jobs>Losses are typically carried forward to the next year and must be recovered before bonuses are paid. At firms like Millennium, salaries may also be treated as an advance against future profits.
This is why a period of deep losses is often followed by a rush to join new funds with a clean slate. Excepting the names above, we could therefore be in for a period of high PM liquidity in London.
Or not. The head of one pod said many people are getting tapped on the shoulder. "But the problem with a year like this is that with lots of PMs down, you fire one and hire another guy who lost money as well."

item.title: It seems some more credit people left Mizuho in London
item.description:
As we have written </news/mizuho-s-london-traders-have-got-a-temporary-new-york-boss-two-more-left>, credit salespeople and traders keep leaving Mizuho's European business. This is occurring still.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Following the exits of Vikram Dadlani </news/ex-deutsche-bank-trader-with-a-big-new-job-is-out-after-a-year>, who joined from Deutsche Bank to run EMEA credit trading in September 2025 and of Asif Godall </news/mizuho-traders-leaving>, who hired him and left in May, plus many others, we understand that Mizuho has waved more goodbyes.
Mizuho isn't commenting and neither are the individuals concerned, but multiple sources say that Rob Samuels, the head of UK credit sales at Mizuho, is on his way to Santander. Santander did not respond to a request to confirm this. Samuels is still registered with Mizuho on the FCA Register.
At the same time, we understand that senior credit researcher Philippe Landroit, who left SocGen in June and arrived at Mizuho earlier this month according the FCA Register, is also leaving. This has not been confirmed with Landroit, who didn't respond to requests to comment. He too is still registered as working for Mizuho by the regulator.
Mizuho's London credit business is in the clutch of change. New York-based David Moore has been appointed </news/mizuho-s-london-traders-have-got-a-temporary-new-york-boss-two-more-left>interim head of global markets for EMEA. Moore flies in and out.

item.title: What you need to know about fintech stock pay today: "Everything is up for discussion"
item.description:
The greatest appeal of joining a budding start-up </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-fintech>is often equity pay </news/how-much-do-fintech-startup-jobs-really-pay>, with lucrative upside if the company grows to be worth billions of dollars. Today, as valuations in major AI labs </news/the-difference-between-working-as-a-quant-in-finance-and-as-a-researcher-in-an-ai-lab>balloon and quant firms </news/pay-for-electronic-trading-graduates-is-soaring-1m-at-hrt-850k-at-jane-street>offer $1m compensation packages right out of the gate, the risks of joining a start-up are starting to seem much greater than the rewards. Industry experts speaking at the Sifted Summit last week have described how companies are changing their approach to equity compensation in order to fight back.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
"This is not a playbook era," said Michelle Coventry, VP of talent for VC fund Creandum. "Anything to do with equity compensation is up for discussion." Four-year vesting periods, </news/fintech-culture-and-stock-pay> which have historically been popular, aren't viable for certain roles where the average tenure is falling; Coventry said that top go-to-market professionals now stay at start-ups for just "24 to 26 months" on average. She said that start-ups are having to take "creative approaches" to accommodate these hires because "everyone wants something different."
The nature of exit opportunities has changed too. Katie Conn, an investment manager for VC firm </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-venture-capital>Salica Investments, said that the "IPO market </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm> has been fairly quiet and M&A </news/get-a-job-in-ma>hasn't filled that gap." This is not always due to a lack of success in the businesses; Mike Turner, partner in the M&A practice of Latham & Watkins, said that "companies are able to stay private for longer and choosing to [do so]," due to an abundance of late-stage growth capital.
To keep employees engaged, and to give them an opportunity to cash out stock, secondary share sales have exploded in popularity over the past few years. These used to be frowned upon, as they signalled you weren't close to an exit; Coventry said that "secondaries used to be a dirty word," while Crowdcube CEO Matt Cooper said that conversations on secondaries used to happen in "dark rooms with hushed tones." Today, they have become a status symbol of the fastest-rising start-ups, and a chance to update your firm's valuation.
Fintechs have been at the forefront of this. Revolut has more than doubled its valuation <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revoluts-rise-become-europes-115-billion-big-bank-rival-2026-10-04/> in the past two years using secondary sales. Stripe's valuation was cut in half to $50bn <https://www.reuters.com/technology/fintech-stripe-valued-50-bln-after-65-bln-fundraise-2023-03-15/> during its last primary fundraising round in 2023, but it achieved a valuation of $159bn <https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/24/stripe-value-stock-sale-tender-offer.html> during a secondary share sale this February.
Employees don't reap the maximum benefit from these share sales. Manish Prayaga, founder of cap table management platform Terraledge, told us that employees often sell their shares "at quite a steep discount on the headline valuation for that company" during a secondaries transaction. The discount can be as much as 30 to 50 percent.
The discount isn't as steep for established companies; Prayaga said that, "obviously, a series B company is higher risk than Anthropic, which is much later stage, so the level of discount is proportional to that." He said that secondary sales are still very attractive to startup employees because you can wait "for an exit event which might take a couple more years… or you could use that money to put a deposit down on a house.”
You might even get a better deal than you would if you wait for an IPO. One fintech startup founder, speaking to us anonymously, said "there's a huge bubble in private markets right now versus public... the money is just flowing right now and I think a lot of startups are exploiting it." Private markets dictate valuations up to the point of an IPO, but then employees with stock have to wait out an excruciating six-month lockup period. </news/ex-barclays-and-morgan-stanley-bankers-holding-millions-at-figma-face-an-awkward-5-months>

item.title: Morning Coffee: How Citi is managing the most awkward bit of its new analyst program. The new technology interviews
item.description:
As we noted yesterday </news/now-citi-will-promote-even-its-moderately-good-analysts-to-associate-after-two-years>, Citi has begun promoting its analysts to associates in two years instead of three. Citi was promoting some analysts to associates in two years previously, but only the very best ones. Now, everyone will be expedited. Good times indeed!
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Unless, of course, you're a current third year Citi analyst, about to become an associate, in which case you might look askance at the newly promoted associates with up to a third less experience than you and wonder whether their AI prompting skills are really sufficient to close the gap.
Citi appears to have thought of this issue. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-05/citi-speeds-junior-bankers-ascent-in-fight-with-private-equity>reported yesterday that Citi's current third year analysts will be promoted to associate as usual on January 1st. By comparison, the second year analysts who are being promoted early to associates will probably not get the call until around July 2027.
In this way, the current third years will get a whole year of associate salaries and associate bonuses, whereas the expedited second years will only get six months. Effectively, they are being promoted six months early.
Bloomberg says the move is to stop Citi's juniors leaving for the likes of private equity, but some senior Citi insiders say there's been a constant dribbling out of analysts and associates this year that needed to be stemmed. Shortening the analyst program could help, although Bloomberg notes that January's associate promotions will be 'subject to performance,' implying that nothing is guaranteed.
Separately, TechCrunch <https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/05/hackerranks-ai-interviewer-offers-a-glimpse-into-what-job-interviews-could-become/?utm_medium=organic_social&utm_source=TWITTER> reports that HackerRank </news/2020/12/coding-interviews-hackerrank-nightmare>, the coding test company that has long been the bane of anyone attempting to get a technology job in banking has developed a new product called Chakra.
This does not refer to a crystal with the ability to solve the Trapping Rain Water Problem </news/2023/02/goldman-sachs-leetcode-problem>, but to a new and dynamic system in which you work through a coding task using a code repository and an AI assistant ("Chakra") that keeps asking what you're doing and introducing new constraints. Sounds great.
Meanwhile...
Citi will also end its fixed-term employment provision that typically applied to investment banking analysts in North America, meaning those employees no longer have a pre-determined contractual end date. (Financial Times) < https://www.ft.com/content/41b567dc-50e9-4c41-95bb-e295caaf2340?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Citi is now the top underwriter for IPOs globally (based on the first nine months of the year). Vis Raghavan will be proud. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-06/citi-takes-top-spot-in-global-ipo-underwriting-through-september?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261006&utm_campaign=author_16891741>
Dwayne Lysaght says JPMorgan has a "growth mindset" in European investment banking. “We want to instil the mentality that you should not be content to win the race by one second, but by a distance,” said his co-head, Alberto Piana. (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/jpmorgans-new-european-dealmaking-bosses-we-want-to-win-by-a-distance-e4a12948>
Global M&A revenues also appear to be slowing down. They were $1.7t in Q2 and $986bn in Q3. (Financial Times) <https://www.ft.com/content/00fb4438-1f86-4bf2-a165-0c39f3fd506b?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
TRex Bio Inc., an early-stage biotech focused on autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, wants to raise up to $133.3m in an IPO. JPMorgan, Evercore, Cantor Fitzgerald, Stifel and Wedbush PacGrow are working on it. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-05/eli-lilly-backed-trex-bio-seeks-to-raise-133-3-million-in-ipo?taid=6ac3c729b459b60001b7f9e6&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
A woman who became a JPMorgan MD aged 29 is selling her $37bn Palmer Square CLO business </news/jp-morgan-md-29> to Goldman Sachs for an unspecified price, and now everyone wants to buy a CLO business for the lucrative flow of fees from deals already created. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-05/goldman-s-bid-for-clo-manager-highlights-wall-street-s-fee-hunt?taid=6ac3bdc9c39c650001a4dea6&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>)
Three years ago, Dmitry Balyasny took over Balyasny's equities business. Now things have been shaken up and star Balyasny stock picker Ilan Weiss has been promoted to co-head of equities alongside him. Weiss's team has generated the highest profits in the equities business. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-05/balyasny-elevates-star-stock-picker-weiss-to-co-lead-equities?taid=6ac3cbdab459b60001b7fa3f&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Hedge funds like Taula and Balyasny had piled into carry trades to profit from the difference between interest-rate swaps and French yields. They had to unwind these quickly last Thursday when French bonds slumped. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/hedge-funds-exiting-crowded-trades-fueled-rout-in-french-bonds>
Critical things to consider when you're writing your CV now. What is the hardest-to-fake evidence that you are good? What have you built or done that gives the interviewer something concrete to ask about? (YoungandCalculated) <https://youngandcalculated.substack.com/p/the-quant-resume-that-actually-gets?utm_source=post-email-title&publication_id=4607221&post_id=218931493&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=k3np9&triedRedirect=true&utm_medium=email>
A retired City lawyer, who lives in Wandsworth, south London paid £2k in council tax last year. In April 2028 his bills will rise to almost £9k. "I’ve paid my taxes all my working life, and hoped that my savings could benefit my five children and grandchildren.” (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/money/tax/article/my-tax-bill-will-go-up-7000-the-london-borough-facing-record-rises-8x6zgwxps>
Mamdani: “Socialism to me means you’ll have whatever you need to live a dignified life and that it is the government’s job to deliver on that.... When people say dignity we’re talking about the things that allow you to take a breath. Housing, child care, public transit. No one should be priced out of these things. These are nonnegotiables, you need these to live.” (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/opinion/free-expression/under-socialism-dignity-is-an-impossible-dream-4e47a4fb?mod=e2tw>

item.title: Hudson River Trading hired an executive from an eco-friendly high-performance computing firm
item.description:
Will the battle for alpha among quant traders </news/quant-jobs-finance> be decided by whoever has the best data centre? Hedge funds and algorithmic trading firms alike </news/data-centres-hedge-funds>are hiring hardware specialists just in case. At Hudson River Trading, </news/the-coffee-run-the-kind-trading-firm-paying-1m-to-graduates-and-100m-to-its-top-people>which has been known to let its traders spend up to $1k a day on tokens </news/ai-token-use-traders>, the latest arrival in this space is a former executive of a publicly traded high-performance computing firm.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
HRT hired Harry McHugh as a systems engineer, based in Singapore according to his LinkedIn profile. He spent the last two years as chief information officer of DUG, an Australian technology firm that provides cloud-based high-performance computing services similar to those on offer by 'neoclouds' like CoreWeave. DUG touts a proprietary immersion cooling system <https://dug.com/dug-cool/> that can cut data centre water usage by up to 25%.
McHugh also spent three and a half years with hardware manufacturer AMD, where he was a senior member of technical staff working on semiconductors. He joined after a previous stint at DUG, where he was head of high-performance computing.
He'll have his work cut out for him at Hudson River Trading which, like most quant firms, has been building a colossal hardware stack. The firm has stated in job listings that it has "triple-digit petabyte-scale storage and massive CPU and GPU clusters </news/programming-languages-machine-learning-ai-quant> in globally distributed data centers." In its UK entity, HRT spent £2.4m per head </news/hudson-river-trading-pay-uk-high-frequency-trading>on new equipment last year, roughly triple its spending on compensation. In August, Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/hudson-river-signs-multibillion-dollar-coreweave-crwv-deal-for-ai-cloud>reported that it also entered a multi-billion-dollar agreement with neocloud provider CoreWeave.
Elsewhere in Asia, Goldman Sachs has been bolstering its own electronic trading division. It hired Ross Whittaker as an MD and head of APAC algo trading. He was previously head of pan-Asian electronic execution at Citi, but left in July. </news/another-electronic-equities-md-exited-citi>

item.title: Multiple portfolio managers said to be leaving BlueCrest, including 26-year-old star
item.description:
It's been a difficult year for macro hedge funds </news/2021/05/how-to-get-a-job-in-a-global-macro-fund>, and a particularly difficult September. Against this backdrop, various portfolio managers appear to have left BlueCrest Capital Management, for reasons that are unclear.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
BlueCrest didn't respond to multiple requests to comment for this article. Nor did the portfolio managers concerned, but we understand that around 10 people have either left recently or are leaving.
The departures are thought to include Ben Turner, the 26 year-old ex-Barclays </news/barclays-macro-to-hedge-funds>sterling rates trader who became a BlueCrest partner on May 1st </news/ben-turner-bluecrest>. Turner is still registered at BlueCrest with the FCA, however. The FCA Register shows Robert Robinson, who joined from Hudson River Trading, leaving the UK entity on September 25th. Others, like Tom Bowden (now at Wellington) and Ankur Aneja </news/bluecrest-hiring-traders-from-banks>left earlier this year. Ben Atlas left and went to ExodusPoint.
The departures from BlueCrest may be partly voluntary, but come after top macro portfolio managers at multiple major funds are thought to have had a challenging September. This includes, but is by no means limited to, Taula Capital Management. </news/diego-megia-taula-capital>
BlueCrest had 46 London partners last time it filed accounts. It paid them an average of £959k each in the year to March 2025. </news/bluecrest-london-pay>
Many of those leaving are thought to have come from BlueCrest's rates trading business, which is run by Joseph Walkrush from Miami.

item.title: Now Citi will promote even its moderately good analysts to associate after two years
item.description:
How long will it take you to progress from analyst to associate </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds>in an investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> team? This depends upon how good you are and where you work.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
If you work for Citi, you will now be lucky indeed. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-05/citi-speeds-junior-bankers-ascent-in-fight-with-private-equity?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261005&utm_campaign=author_21835441>reports that Citi is shortening the length of its analyst program to two years, after which all analysts will be transformed into beautiful associates.
Bloomberg says Citi's analyst program previously ran for three years. David Friedland, co-head of North America investment banking, told Bloombeg the truncation of the three year program will bring Citi in line with some competitors. It will also enable Citi analysts to earn higher pay, sooner. Bloomberg suggests the change will discourage these analysts from leaving for private equity and notes that it will now be possible to go from analyst to vice president (VP) at Citi within the blink of five and a half years.
All of this sounds appealing, but it's also worth noting that none of this is entirely new. We reported in 2019 </news/2019/03/analyst-to-associate-to-vp-investment-banks>that Citi, UBS, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were promoting analysts to associates after two years. At that point they'd already been doing it for a while. Goldman Sachs, for example, began promoting analysts to associate in 2016. </news/2016/08/goldman-sachs-early-associate-promotions>
So what's new? Citi declined to comment, but we understand from senior insiders at the bank that the key change is the breadth of the two year program at Citi. Previously, only the very best analysts were promoted to associate after two years. Now, it seems that all Citi analysts will be.
UBS is thought to have a similar approach. So is Goldman Sachs. </news/2021/05/ubs-associate-bonus>
First year analysts at all banks earn around $160k in total compensation. </news/banking-pay>Third year analysts earn around $200k. However, first year associates earn around $276k, so Citi's third year analysts may effectively receive a $76k pay rise.
Curiously, the promotions come at a moment in time when private equity firms are struggling to exit investments, suggesting competition for junior talent may be less fierce than in the past. They also come as AI is being used to do the jobs of junior bankers </news/ai-in-ma-banking>, suggesting that fewer and higher calibre juniors may be the way forward.

item.title: Citi hired a new chief technology officer from UBS
item.description:
Citi's CTO David Griffiths </news/citi-s-cto-says-these-are-the-kinds-of-jobs-he-s-eliminating-with-ai> had a change of role this summer, becoming the bank's group head of artificial intelligence. </news/citi-s-ai-driven-productivity-boom-spells-hard-times-for-banking-contractors>The bank has now appointed his successor, and he comes from UBS.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Paul McEwen joined Citi as chief technology </news/how-to-get-a-technology-job-bank> officer and head of infrastructure, based in New York. He spent the last 12 and a half years at UBS in a variety of senior roles including global head of technology services, as well as group head of infrastructure and security engineering. In the middle of that stint, he left for Wells Fargo, where he worked for seven months as its head of infrastructure before returning to UBS.
McEwan is a citi alum. He was at the bank from 2000 to 2006 and served as global head of applications. He also spent eight years at JPMorgan where he was CTO of client services.
As head of infrastructure, McEwen will presumably work alongside Griffiths on Arc, Citi's internal agentic platform <https://time.com/collection/executives-of-the-year-tech-data/2026/david-griffiths/#:~:text=Arc%2C%20Citi%E2%80%99s%20internal,bank%2C%E2%80%9D%20Griffiths%20says.> which launched earlier this year. McEwen wrote in an article earlier this year that UBS has been working on AI agents too and is "seeing promising results... in areas such as triaging security alerts, clearing tickets that pile up, and creating incident closure summaries." UBS and Citi declined to comment.
UBS isn't the only European bank that lost a senior technologist to an American bank this month. Li Yang, global head of structured products technology for Barclays, left to join Wells Fargo, where he will work as head of structured derivatives technology.

item.title: Citadel Securities rescued a dispossessed marketer for its equity sales team
item.description:
To paraphrase Rhett Butler in Gone with the Wind, there is more good hiring to be done when a hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> fails than when one succeeds. The latest blockade runner, on the buy-side at least, is Citadel Securities.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Brant Duber joined Citadel Securities’ franchise sales team in New York two weeks ago. Duber joined the firm from hedge fund Eminence Capital </news/2023/03/goldman-sachs-program-trading>, the $7bn hedge fund founded and run by Ricky Sandler, where he was director of marketing. Eminence Capital was wound up earlier this year by Sandler due to a sustained period of “underperformance and rising structural challenges”, Business Times reported <https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/banking-finance/ricky-sandler-shuttering-eminence-capital-after-27-year-run>.
Before Eminence Capital, which he joined in 2023, Duber spent 15 years in Goldman Sachs’ equities team. He was made a managing director in its class of 2021 promotions </news/2021/11/goldman-sachs-mds-2021>.
Eminence Capital’s former employees have been dispersed into many corners of the financial services industry. Luke Brzozowski, for example, was a consumer staples portfolio manager at the firm; he’s since gone to Rokos. Nicholas Freymuth, a quantitative developer at the defunct firm, became CTO of $35bn long-only fund Eagle Capital Management.
As far as we can tell, Duber is the only one who has left for Citadel or Citadel Securities. Neither he nor Citadel Securities responded to a request for comment.

item.description:

item.title: Stripe raised headcount and salaries in London last year despite layoffs
item.description:
Payments giant Stripe </news/stripe-has-put-an-ex-hsbc-compliance-guy-in-charge-of-its-uk-office> has big plans for London. 2025 accounts released for the fintech </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-fintech> show that headcount grew significantly over last year; average salaries increased too, but total compensation fell.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Stripe increased its headcount from 288 in 2024 to 340 last year. This is despite the fact that the fintech cut ~3.5% of its global workforce </news/stripe-engineers-on-940k-lament-losing-their-jobs-after-receiving-a-duck-photo> (roughly 300 people) at the start of the year. The fintech opened a new London office in 2024; John Collison told Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-21/stripe-opens-city-of-london-office-to-step-up-uk-expansion> at the time that it has space for 250 employees, suggesting that much of Stripe's UK headcount might work remotely.
Headcount in the UK entity grew by 18%, slightly above the 17% headcount growth that chief people officer Rob McIntosh said that Stripe was aiming for in 2025. <https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/45358/stripe-lays-off-300-employees#:~:text=Stripe%20had%20around%208500%20employees%20before%20the%20latest%20move%20but%20still%20plans%20to%20increase%20its%20headcount%20by%2017%25%20to%2010%2C000%20by%20the%20end%20of%20the%20year%2C%20say%20McIntosh.> The growth was split almost evenly between its administration, sales and engineering divisions. Headcount in user operations slightly fell.
Average total compensation was £247.5k. It was down year on year due to a ~28% decrease in 'other compensation', which includes equity pay. At the same time, 'salaries and wages' increased from £168k to £181k. The number of people who received bonuses last year </news/almost-everyone-got-a-2025-bonus-at-stripe-in-london-almost-no-one-got-a-bonus-at-starling-bank>also slightly decreased, which may have affected average total compensation.
The London office is a fraction of the size of Stripe's Dublin headquarters. The Irish Times <https://www.irishtimes.com/business/2026/10/02/stripe-to-add-200-jobs-at-dublin-headquarters-in-endorsement-of-irish-talent/> reported last week that Stripe's Dublin headcount has increased by more than 35% this year after tripling its office size in 2025.

item.title: Morning Coffee: "Soul-crushing" banking internship vs. $750k on Polymarket. Bad luck for the bankers expecting the biggest bonuses
item.description:
If you're a university student without a banking internship </news/internship-investment-bank>, a university student who's completed a banking internship and found it unedifying, or even a student who's graduated without a top class degree, take heed. There is an alternative. It's lucrative, but it's gruelling.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/ac1f4db2-54fe-4a36-b3db-bb96675231f5>says a small group of elite and highly competitive students are making a fortune on Polymarket. They are mostly Gen Z and are at top universities. They are the sorts of bookish children and Olympiad winners who typically join top banks or top electronic trading firms. There are 30 of them on a Discord server called Alpha and in two years they've made a collective $40m.
The students in question bet on everything from the weather, to US elections, to victories and defeats in the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Their bets are not "dumb" and they do not rely upon luck. They are highly researched and considered. It helps to be an adept at "building probabilistic models from vast historic datasets." It also helps to be able to click your mouse at high speeds.
It's harder to get into Alpha than it is to get a banking internship. The group is invitation only and invitations depend upon becoming known to the group, often via pertinent observations on other Discords. These observations must be deleted upon joining. By keeping ideas for bets inside Alpha, knowledge is pooled. Outside, it drains away.
One recent Oxford University graduate told the FT he spent so much time researching bets and trading on Polymarket that he eventually graduated with a 2.2. However, he also graduated with $750k in the bank. He completed an internship at a small investment bank in his first year at university but found it "soul-crushing and alienating." In his second summer, he had no internship but was deep in Alpha.
Making money on Polymarket isn't easy. Some of the Alpha members the FT spoke to intimated addiction and relationship-breakdowns. “It sucks you in, especially if you’re capable,” said one. “It definitely consumes my life in a way that is not positive.”
The Oxford University graduate said it became difficult to write essays because his brain became accustomed to clicking, prompting and scrolling. He went on holiday with his girlfriend at Easter and spent hours each day clicking between Polymarket and Discord. But now he's graduated and has $750k in the bank. He's interrailing through Europe. He's meeting his girlfriend in Thailand. He's still trading on Polymarket, but less intensely than before. There are no plans to go into banking.
Separately, equity capital markets (ECM) bankers have been predicted </news/2026-bonuses-finance>to receive generous bonuses for most of 2026. Maybe this will no longer occur.
The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/b8924d77-364b-46c1-b783-5db73a91f351?syn-25a6b1a6=1>notes that IPO proceeds so far this year have hit $147.5bn, versus $44bn for the same period last year, but that the engine is starting to sputter.
A long list of companies that were planning to IPO in the third or fourth quarters have had second thoughts. They include OpenAI, EG Group, Holtec, Oura, SB Energy, Bamboo Insurance, Anthropic, AS Watson, Waterstones and Loveholidays. Ennismore and Hotel Investment Partners may yet delay IPOs too. Anthropic is going ahead, likely in November, but there is some trepidation.
Part of the problem is that some of this year's earlier IPOs (SpaceX) have since plummeted in value. The big question now is whether 2026's delayed IPOs will happen in 2027. It's also whether ECM bankers will get paid as much as they'd hoped or whether banks will use the softening and postponements as an excuse to direct money elsewhere.
Meanwhile...
Legal500 produced an annual league table of barristers. It went live with scathing reviews thanks to a work experience student with a grudge. (RollonFriday) <https://www.rollonfriday.com/news-content/exclusive-legal500-accidentally-publishes-terrible-reviews-top-barristers>
“I arrived to start my first year of university in September, and by the end of October all my course mates had spring weeks secured — I did not even know what a spring week was.” (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/business/companies-markets/article/graduates-shake-up-the-status-quo-in-financial-services-xzgdxwb9t?t=1791141141721>
Citadel Securities bought a stake in Wolfe Research and now its clients will get access to Wolfe's research and it will execute trades for Wolfe's clients. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/citadel-securities-buys-stake-in-wolfe-research-for-trading-flow?taid=6abfcbab9f70760001f22f71&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
QRT hired Adhitya Sethaputra, a commodities trader who left Radiant World. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/qrt-hires-metals-trader-sethaputra-after-radiant-world-departure?taid=6ac01a2cadc2d20001479e0e&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
When you're a VC with a passion for boasting on X. "Very "light" Saturday with 7 meetings on the calendar, working and coding in between. Loving the times..." (X) <https://x.com/alexiskold/status/2106413277588643960>
A whistleblower who flagged Howard Lutnick's ties to Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide according to the Banker. There is no suggestion that the two things are connected. Simon Andriesz spent 35 years in fixed income trading in London. Lutnick has denied any wrongdoing and said previously that: "I unequivocally condemn the conduct attributed to Jeffrey Epstein and everyone who participated in his illegal activities. The survivors of his crimes deserve our respect and support.” (The Banker) <https://www.thebanker.com/content/02286d53-0338-42ef-996d-5f7712b9f133>

item.title: Buy-side jobs in Asia: Who's feeling the effects of AI the most?
item.description:
Getting a job on the buy side has always been hard but AI has made it even harder for a lot of people. Some roles at hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> and private equity </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-private-equity> firms in Asia are faring better than they are elsewhere. June Tan, head of buy-side non-investment hiring at recruitment firm Principle Partners, spoke to us in advance of her AMA on The Bubble <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/t/recruiter-ama-finance-and-middle-office-principle-partners-pte/6063/11>, our new anonymous forum, to discuss how attitudes towards hiring have changed as a result of technological advances.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Anonymous headhunters have told us that, in Europe and the US, operations staff who are non-technical are under serious threat and get "replaced by automation on a weekly basis." </news/how-hedge-funds-use-ai> Tan said that they're "not being let go" in Asia; "they still have value and are still here." AI has, however, created increased demand for "junior candidates with tech skills... not really native Python </news/python-libraries-for-finance>coders, but people who appreciate the language." Operations </news/operations-jobs-banking> staff who are adept coders "are more popular in quant funds </news/biggest-quant-hedge-funds> than traditional hedge funds."
If not operations, who is at risk? Tan said that finance divisions in hedge funds are "most exposed" to AI because they're "highly dependent on data reporting and will use these [AI] tools immediately." Another function at risk is compliance, which "needs to deal with similarly large sets of data." There are bright spots; Tan said quant funds are "trying to set up trading surveillance functions" and "need people to build the infrastructure rather than a project manager who can just interact with vendors."
When answering preliminary questions in the AMA, Tan said that she doesn't expect functions like compliance and operations to be replaced, but "the nature of the roles will certainly change." If you're unable to learn how to use AI tools and new technologies, "there is a real risk of becoming less relevant."
For private equity firms, the state of hiring is quite different. There are very few growth areas, and most of the hiring is "just musical chairs" as firms look to replace employees that leave. One of the brightest areas is investor relations. Tan said this is the "only vibrant function," and that PE firms are "hiring junior and mid-level guys to help them with fundraising." Tan said there's also a "slight increase in demand for internal audit professionals, largely driven by investors looking into companies and wanting to do a bit more due diligence."
Want to ask June something about buy-side or middle-office jobs in APAC? She'll be holding an AMA in The Bubble on the 6th of October; you can post your questions here. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/t/recruiter-ama-finance-and-middle-office-principle-partners-pte/6063/9>

item.title: Another banking MD left Citi, this time for Barclays
item.description:
Ali Akram, one of Citi's most popular London managing directors, has resurfaced at Barclays.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Akram, who ran the business services sector team at Citi in London, arrived at Barclays today according to a post on his LinkedIn profile. He didn't respond to a request to comment for this article and neither Barclays nor Citi immediately commented. The FCA Register shows Akram leaving Citi at the end of July.
Akram joined Citi from UBS in 2016 and is thought to have built the services team there. He's understood to have been one of Citi's strongest and well-liked sector bankers in Europe.
Akram's arrival at Barclays coincides with that of Greg Dalle, the co-head of Citi's EMEA industrials group. Dalle also officially left Citi at the end of July according to the FCA Register. Dalle is now the co-head of EMEA industrials at Barclays. Akram will run the business services team at the UK bank. Mike Lamb also returned to Barclays from Citi in February and is chairman of the financial institutions group in EMEA.
Citi has embarked upon a banker hiring spree under Vis Raghavan </news/citi-paid-vis-raghavan-25m-to-hire-from-jp-morgan-jp-morgan-paid-doug-petno-23m-to-hire-from-citi>, who's been running the investment bank since 2024. Raghavan said in May </news/citi-investor-day-2026> that he had made 60 new hires, that he can hire whomever he likes, <https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/whoever-want-citis-investment-banking-160217983.html> and that he planned to continue doing so. Many of the people he likes are his former colleagues from JPMorgan.
Dealogic says Citi ranked outside the top ten in both the UK and EMEA for M&A revenues in the first nine months of 2026. It ranked 8th globally for M&A over the same period, down from 6th last year.

item.title: An ex-MD at JPMorgan has gone public about her horrific marriage
item.description:
Kathryn Benwell is no longer a managing director (MD) at JPMorgan in London. She left the bank over 10 years ago in October 2015. Eleven years later, Benwell has begun explaining just how difficult her life was during that time.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Benwell spent nearly a decade working for JPMorgan in London and became an MD at the bank in 2011. She began her career as a regulator, working for the Bank of England the Financial Services Authority. During her tenure as a JPMorgan MD she worked in risk and controls, improving governance arrangements for the bank's legal entities.
From 2013, though, Benwell was in a highly abusive relationship. We haven't spoken to her for this article, but Benwell - who is now a self employed operational resilience specialist and ambassador for a domestic abuse charity - featured in a Channel 4 documentary <https://www.channel4.com/programmes/paul-c-brunson-red-flag/on-demand/80694-004> this week detailing how she became immersed in a relationship with a violent man.
After her previous 30-year marriage ended, Benwell said she went on a dating app aged 47 and "was swept along on a romance" with a 6 foot four blue-eyed property developer who seemed like he would protect her. "I wanted a dominant, alpha type guy that I could look up to," said Benwell. She was warned by friends that he had a history of violence towards his previous partners, and even his mother told her not to trust him, but in both cases he undermined the testimony of the women who were telling her to be careful.
After moving the unnamed man into her large new house in Kent, Benwell married him in April 2015. She was already supporting him as he never seemed to have any money. Her son was away at university; her daughter was moved against her will into a static caravan in the grounds. Her new husband slowly became increasingly violent. Benwell constantly excused his behaviour, until eventually he nearly killed her and broke her back. In 2023, she finally went to the police. He was sentenced to two years in prison in 2024, but released after five months due to prison overcrowding.
Writing on LinkedIn, Benwell said: "At work I had all the pressure of a 24-7 global role. At home I wanted to relax with someone who looked after me, someone bigger than me, someone strong and dominant so that I didn’t need to be in charge."
Initially, Benwell said her abuser was a gentleman. "He drove me to the station and made sure I sat in first class, texting me to make sure I had got a seat and sending loving emojis on my journey. When I got back he was standing on the platform with an umbrella to shield me if it was raining. He held my hand and opened doors for me. He drove me everywhere and took me out to dinner after work."
In fact, he was a controlling, violent despot. Over time, his behaviour changed. He stopped opening doors and started flying into a rage about tiny things. "I would have to run out of client meetings at 5pm sharp to get back to him on time otherwise he would be angry at being kept waiting....If I worked at home he would stand in the doorway tapping on his watch if a meeting went past 5pm. I cringed with embarrassment as he loomed behind me in Teams meetings."
Speaking to the Daily Mail, <https://www.dailymail.com/lifestyle/article-16164573/JP-Morgan-banker-husband-violence.html> Benwell said: “This happened to a man­aging dir­ector at JPMor­gan. If you think it’s not hap­pen­ing to people here, think again. I’m a liv­ing, walk­ing example of domestic abuse."

item.title: Apollo is still paying great in London. KKR is still paying good
item.description:
Working at a huge private equity </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-private-equity> or private credit </news/private-credit> firm has its perks. The pay packages can still be attractive, even if they’ve been a bit meagre recently </news/private-equity-credit-compensation>, and some firms have still been hiring strongly.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
2025 UK accounts released earlier this week for Apollo and KKR offered an insight into just how attractive they can be, through their companies house registered firms, Apollo Management International LLP (Apollo) and Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. Partners LLP (KKR).
Both firms did pretty well. Revenue at Apollo went from $467m in 2024 to $657m in 2025, a 40% increase, and at KKR they went from £150m ($199m) to £177m ($234m), an 18% increase. Operating profit was up to, by 15% at Apollo and 8% at KKR. Both subsidiaries outperformed their parent companies' global performances.
Both firms, accordingly, increased headcount. Apollo went from 301 people to 340 people in the UK across 2025, and KKR went from 169 people to 182 during the year. Interestingly, at Apollo the increase was driven solely by an increase in admin, with the number of “investment professionals” decreasing; at KKR, it was “executives and associates” that grew in number, while admin-related employees declined.
Pay is where things get more complicated. On paper, Apollo paid around $618k per head to its staff in 2025, up from the $521k it paid on average in 2024. KKR, meanwhile, paid “only” around £196k ($259k) in 2025, although that was also up from the £171k ($226k) it paid on average in 2024.
Things were complicated by each firm’s members (UK legal jargon for partners in a partnership). Despite being half the size of Apollo on paper, KKR had three times as many members – 27 for Apollo, and 88 for KKR, up from 28 and 95 last year, respectively.
Apollo’s 27 partners earned an average of $6.5m each for their work in 2025, up from the $5.7m they earned on average for 2024. That figure includes a large $20m lump sum in 2025 to “the member with the largest entitlement,” which was $169m last year. This is very possibly Apollo’s US parent company.
At KKR, the firm’s 88 members included two corporate members. Discounting these, the firm paid out just £327k ($432k) to its individual members in 2025, and £308k ($407k) each in 2024. KKR’s parent company, meanwhile, received £21m ($28m).

item.title: Morning Coffee: Ex-HSBC banker paid circa $1.4m destroyed career while saving money. A great time to work for a quant fund
item.description:
These are straitened times. Costs are high and rising and anecdotally there are many well paid people in financial services who expected rates to remain low and are now nursing large increases in mortgage repayments.
It's not clear whether Joseph Molloy </news/hsbc-banker-fare-evasion>, a former head of passive equity at HSBC asset management, who has a £2m house in Orpington Kent, was facing ejection from his low fixed rate mortgage. But Molloy did want to save money. He is the man who rode the trains in and out of London for nearly a year and didn't pay the full fare. Molloy was caught, banned from South Eastern railway for 12 months and given a suspended sentence in February.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Yesterday, the FCA also banned Molloy - who'd worked in financial services for at least two decades - from ever working in financial services again. It's an ignominious end to a career in which he rose the ranks at State Street, Northern Trust and Legal and General before joining HSBC to acclaim in 2015. <https://etfexpress.com/2015/03/23/joseph-molloy-joins-hsbc-global-asset-management-head-passives/> It's not clear how much Molloy was earning at HSBC, but given that the bank paid its material risk takers (MRTs) at Molloy's level an average of $1.4m last year, </news/hsbc-is-paying-senior-bankers-who-stay-1-4m-and-senior-bankers-who-go-500k>this would seem a reasonable guess.
Now, Molloy - who is aged 53 and retired last year - won't be earning $1.4m, Nor will he need to travel to HSBC or any other bank in London. In banning him <https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/final-notices/joseph-molloy-2026.pdf> from working in financial services again, the FCA said Molloy's actions demonstrated "a clear and serious lack of honesty and integrity such that he is not fit and proper to perform regulated activities."
The FCA also elaborated upon Molloy's techniques for saving money on his train fares. These were very involved. First, he "dishonestly acquired travel cards using two separate accounts with Southeastern with false names, addresses and email accounts." Then, he "paid for a short journey at the start and end of each journey but evaded the fare for the section of the journey in between." In this way, he saved nearly £6k over 740 journeys. The FT <https://www.ft.com/content/ed5aae75-e06b-49bc-8e96-6c596f88f2c7?syn-25a6b1a6=1> says Molloy also achieved a Jobcentre Plus discount card for unemployed people, which gave him 50% off train tickets.
These techniques are usually used by students or the unemployed. Molloy had mitigating circumstances - his mother had recently died, and the judge in February said he was genuinely remorseful. The FCA was less sympathetic. Molloy's fraud was "sophisticated and determined," it said. Molloy was also more than able to pay the full price of the ticket. Now Molloy might have to go by bike instead.
Separately, it's a great time to work for a quant hedge fund </news/biggest-quant-hedge-funds>. The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/75b0ab84-a252-4ea1-9058-c9ee7ca07f4f?syn-25a6b1a6=1> reports that trend following funds like Graham Capital and Winton are having a good year because the trends are so strong. Graham is up more than 31%; Winton's diversified macro fund is up 17.5%.
The trends in question involve inflation, bonds and currencies. Multistrategy </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-hiring> firms are doing less well: Millennium generated zero returns in September. <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-01/millennium-saw-zero-return-in-volatile-september-for-hedge-funds?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261001&utm_campaign=author_19458291>
Meanwhile...
Taula Capital's TSO fund made a large bet on European interest rates going down and lost 12.2% in September alone. Backers can't redeem their capital until next spring. (Business Insider) <https://www.businessinsider.com/taula-capital-september-performance-bond-market-pain-2026-10>
Paramount SkyDance is funding its $110bn purchase of Warner Bros Discovery with $52bn of debt. The new company will have net debt of $80bn and annual ebitda of only $12bn. Investors are demanding a 9% yield on the junk part of the new debt. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/1b5ddda2-ac55-4d66-8bf4-bce62b80450d?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Private equity executives are now being forced to admit that they won't be able to sell the companies they bought in the long era of low interest rates for much (if any?) of a profit. They are sitting on them instead. Human resources company UKG (formerly Kronos Inc.) has been owned by Hellman & Friedman for nearly two decades. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2026-09-30/the-end-of-private-equity-s-leveraged-buyout-era-is-nigh>
Spreads on global corporate bonds have blown out about 5 basis points this week. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/global-credit-market-starts-to-sputter-as-jumbo-deals-drag?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261002&utm_campaign=author_19908303>
Hernán Cristerna, JPMorgan's executive chairman of global investment banking and M&A has decided this is a good time to retire. (Reuters) <https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/jpmorgan-dealmaker-hernan-cristerna-retire-end-of-2026-2026-10-01/>
M&A volume in the Australia has nearly doubled to $55 billion this year. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/asia-bankers-hope-japan-australia-can-lift-m-a-from-doldrums?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261002&utm_campaign=author_16891741>
Anthropic's IPO is expected in November and may be marketed from the week of November 9th. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-01/anthropic-is-said-to-plan-pre-ipo-investor-day-as-listing-nears>
Chris Rokos sold his mansion in Palm Beach County for $83.2 million. In February 2025 he wanted $150m for it. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/real-estate/luxury-homes/chris-rokos-manalapan-florida-home-6722f1ff?mod=hp_major_pos1>
Martin Pabari, COO of Millennium in EMEA, says people must use AI. “The most valuable outcomes come from knowing how to frame a problem, challenging an output, and figuring out how to apply an insight to a practical problem.” (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/millennium-emea-ceos-advice-to-young-talent-embrace-ai-c4d03db6>
Barclays wants 50% of its software developers to be using Claude Code by the end of 2026. Its markets platform receives 120,000 emails a day and already uses Claude to streamline how client inquiries are processed and managed. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-01/barclays-expands-use-of-anthropic-s-claude-in-efficiency-push>
How to save money on tokens: Direct employees to the company’s pre-built library of existing prompts that are optimized to not go overboard with token usage. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/cio-journal/the-complicated-reality-behind-ai-token-limits-10298543>
Putting ADHD disclaimers at the end of emails is a thing. (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/comment/columnists/article/adhd-email-signatures-opportunity-workplace-fad-tpvmv5bct>
Shannon Burns, a technology executive claimed record damages of £76 million after a tribunal found that she suffered discrimination at a company which fired her after she became intoxicated at a work event, locked herself out of a hotel room and was forced to sleep in a sauna. Burns said she was discriminated against because male colleagues were in a similar state. (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/uk/law/article/barrister-01-c87cv07qp>

item.title: The Barclays macro director who's having an enormous year
item.description:
As we reported last week, Barclays has lost more rates sales people. James Hackett </news/another-rates-md-left-barclays-in-london-after-resigning-earlier-this-week>resigned, possibly to join his old colleague Cosimo Codacci-Pisanelli over at Goldman Sachs, although this is not confirmed. Karan Sofat, an up-and-coming junior rates sales guy is also understood to be leaving. Barclays will likely miss them both. However, it is fortunately still equipped with one of the hottest youngish rates sales people in London: Punitha Rajah.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
We have not spoken to Rajah for this article, but multiple Barclays insiders say he is having a monumental year. "He's exploded," says one. "He is probably the top producer now."
Rajah, who is known as "Puni" has been a director at Barclays since 2019. He was promoted in September last year </news/barclays-performed-promotions-to-stop-macro-salespeople-joining-their-friend> and is now thought to be running UK real money sales. Insiders say his ascension has been astonishing and that he will almost certainly be on this year's managing director (MD) list.
Rajah graduated from the UK's University of the West of England, which ranks 39th in the Guardian University Guide and is not among banks' usual target schools. </news/target-universities-finance-uk>He began his career as a trading assistant, working in a support role.
"He came from humble beginnings," says one colleague. "He's worked his way up and it's been very impressive. I've seen tons of grads come and go and Rajah is part of the new generation. He's a mix of old school sales who can pick up the phone, and someone who knows how to entertain clients in the Instagram era."
Rajah's personal Instagram account is part of his appeal. Rajah is a fan of bling and many of his images - mostly tongue in cheek - reflect this. "He's made it and he lives a glam life," says a former colleague. "He has a very bright future and is following in the footsteps of Filippo Zorzoli." </news/barclays-performed-promotions-to-stop-macro-salespeople-joining-their-friend>
Rajah is thought to work alongside Rumit Sawjani, Barclays' longstanding head of hedge funds and institutional rates sales.
We initially said Rajah was 32. In fact, he is understood to be older than this and to have recently celebrated his 40th birthday in lavish style, possibly involving a yacht.

item.title: Drew Gillanders will be hiring for Millennium's new London equities business. Maybe not from Citadel
item.description:
Drew Gillanders, aged 54, is leaving Citadel </news/2022/10/how-to-get-a-job-at-citadel>and joining Millennium. </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium> His exit from Citadel was reported last month. </news/nabeel-bhanji-citadel-equities>Bloomberg reported this week that Gillanders will soon be running a new Millennium business in London focused on international equities under Pete Santoro and Michael Chung.
Gillanders didn't respond to a request to comment for this article. Both Citadel and Millennium declined to comment.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Gillanders hasn't actually arrived at Millennium's UK business yet. He's thought to be on a notice period which is likely to last for at least a year. </news/citadel-non-compete> Since his departure, Citadel's international equities business has been run by 40-year-old </news/nabeel-bhanji-citadel-equities> Nabeel Bhanji <https://www.citadel.com/who-we-are/leadership/nabeel-bhanji/>from Elliott Management. Bhanji joined in November 2025. Citadel restructured its London equities operation and the international equities business run by Gillanders has now been combined with Citadel's "Strategic Equity Investments" team, run by Bhanji.
Gillanders himself spent seven years at Citadel after joining in 2019. As Citadel's head of international equities from 2023, Gillanders is thought to have run a business encompassing 10-15 different portfolios. If this is replicated at Millennium, he could be doing a lot of hiring there.
However, this hiring at Millennium may not involve people from Citadel. Gillanders is likely to be under a non-solicit agreement that will prevent him from recruiting his former colleagues for at least 15 months.
Citadel also operates in a very different way to Millennium. Speaking to London students two years ago, </news/citadel-hedge-fund-jobs-london> Gillanders explained that Citadel takes a long-term view on risk and is able to "take more duration than other funds."
Gillanders elaborated that:
“Some of our peers have a more centralized risk function where if you’re down 2% you have capital taken away from you. This means that you’re having interactions with the risk function when you’re 85 basis points down, and so you’re playing not to lose rather than to win. Your returns in this case will likely be no more than 2% because you never let winners run and you cut losers very tightly.”
This all sounds a bit similar to the approach at Millennium, where risk limits can be famously inflexible. The Wall Street Journal <https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/hedge-fund-millennium-puts-up-an-uncharacteristic-loss-in-february-7a6292b8> reported last year that Millennium can cut teams' capital in half when losses hit 5% and then fire portfolio managers when losses exceed 7.5%. Portfolio managers familiar with the flexy regime at Citadel may not be partial to the Millennium approach.
Gillanders himself will also need to adapt. Millennium's equities business has been co-run by Peter Santoro since 2017. Like Gillanders, Santoro previously worked for Citadel and Morgan Stanley. Unlike Gillanders, who is a former M&A banker and is focused on fundamental investing, Santoro is a career equities trader.
Santoro moved to London last year and has already overseen a build of Millennium's London equities business. In February, he hired Erdit Hoxha, the former co-head of equities at Goldman Sachs, to sit in London within Millennium's 'office of the chief investment officer.' He also added Antoine Foucher from North Rock in December last year to run "equity advisory services." Foucher then hired Dom Duffy from Squarepoint in August.
If you want to work for Millennium's expanding London equities business, you could try hitting up Santoro before Gillanders arrives. Alternatively, there's Sameer Buch </news/hedge-fund-millennium-hired-hedge-fund-schonfeld-s-top-equities-recruiter-in-london>, the London-based fundamental equities business development executive who joined in May.
Santoro and Buch are likely to have hired Gillanders. It's not clear how much Millennium paid </news/millennium-pay-london> for the privilege, but DG was likely earning at least $10m at Citadel in London </news/citadel-london-pay>, even though he wasn't listed as a partner at any of its UK entities from 2021.

item.title: Hudson River Trading hired an ex-Goldman Sachs MD for its growing venture capital arm
item.description:
Want to work as a venture capitalist </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-venture-capital> but not at a venture capital firm? In the past your best bet might have been to work in Goldman Sachs' elite 'principal strategic investments (PSI) group </news/2019/05/the-elite-28-person-goldman-sachs-team-psi>' which, as of 2019 <https://www.cnbc.com/2019/05/03/inside-the-goldman-sachs-tech-fund-that-made-25percent-returns-for-7-years.html>, had invested $1.5bn in 76 companies. Today VC is a space that electronic trading </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> firms are breaking into, and one of the biggest has hired an alum of that elite team in London to help it grow.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Matt O'Neill has joined Hudson River Trading </news/the-coffee-run-the-kind-trading-firm-paying-1m-to-graduates-and-100m-to-its-top-people> in London as an investor with HRT Ventures. HRT's website says that it invests in "early-stage ventures seeking to influence capital markets, trading, and the broader financial landscape." The firm has been making venture investments since at least 2021 <https://www.finews.asia/finance/36642-asset-management-fintech-republic-expands-to-asia#:~:text=Republic%20raised%20%24150,Crunchbase%20data%20show.> when it invested in investment platform Republic. Other investments include AI infrastructure firm Eridu and sports trading platform Sporttrade.
O'Neill was most recently at another trading firm, Flow Traders, where he was global head of business development. He spent three years there, working on relationship management with banks alongside the firm's VC initiatives. Before that, he spent 14 years at Goldman Sachs across two separate stints, where he was an MD and helped set up the PSI group's Hong Kong business. He also spent five years at Morgan Stanley's equities clearing business.
Jane Street has been getting involved in private markets too, most notably by acquiring a stake in Anthropic </news/the-difference-between-working-as-a-quant-in-finance-and-as-a-researcher-in-an-ai-lab> from FTX following its bankruptcy </news/2023/11/sam-bankman-fried-ftx-fallout>. The firm has used these investments as an opportunity to "expand [into] businesses that are more public facing" according to Jane Street trader John Case in an interview with the Wall Street Journal <https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/jane-street-ai-wall-street-bdfcc81a>in June.
The prevalence of trading firms in the VC space may also be influenced by the various trading firm alums who have built successful startups. HRT's first intern class </news/networking-for-1m-quant-and-ai-jobs-really-begins-at-14-years-old> famously included several major players in the AI space today including Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang, Cognition CEO Scott Wu and Hyperliquid </news/jeffrey-yan> founder Jeff Yan.
O'Neill did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Hedge fund Millennium's average pay keeps falling in London as it keeps hiring non-investment staff
item.description:
Working for a big hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> like Millennium can be pretty fun. The firm’s assets under management are growing, and there are jobs paying $100m </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium> going around. Most jobs, though, do not pay this much.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Accounts released earlier this week for Millennium Capital Partners LLP and Millennium Capital Management Ltd, the firm’s main two London subsidiaries, showed that the average employee at Millennium in the UK does not receive a very, very large amount.
Millennium paid its London staff £671k ($892k) on average for the year ending 2025. This was third year in a row that pay declined: from £1.1m ($1.5m) in 2022, to £776k ($1.03m) in 2023, and to £717k ($953k) in 2024. In the past four years, therefore, average pay at Millennium in London has fallen by almost 40%.
This is unlikely to be the result of individual pay cuts. Instead, the firm has been skewing headcount in favour of non-investment staff, who usually cost less money. Last year, for example, the firm cut 31 investment professionals and hired 52 support staff. In the past four years, the percentage of investment staff went from around 55% to around 47%.
Members at Millennium, also known as partners, have fared better. Members are usually senior portfolio managers </news/the-problem-with-hedge-funds-is-that-too-many-portfolio-managers-are-no-good>. Millennium’s London partners earned £8.1m ($10.8m) each on average for their 2025 work, up two-thirds from the £4.9m ($6.5m) they earned on average in 2024, measured as total partner remuneration, divided by the number of partners.
It's worth noting that Millennium Capital Partners LLP has 33 partners, of which two were corporates: Millennium Capital Management Ltd, and MCM (UK) LLC, a Delaware-listed firm. It's possible that a significant chunk of the member profit pot, up to £35m ($47m), went to one of these members. Other London partners include Gauthier Amiot </news/now-ubs-s-global-head-of-exotics-trading-got-a-big-job-at-hedge-fund-millenium>, Millennium's deputy head of global volatility arbitrage, and Nicolas Meiller </news/hedge-fund-millennium-hired-a-trader-who-escaped-from-eisler-and-made-him-a-partner>, formerly an Eisler trader.
Turnover for the group increased to £1.5bn ($2.1bn) in 2025, up from £1.4bn ($1.9bn) in 2024. Operating profit for the year increased more dramatically from £274m ($362m) to £430m ($568m).
Fascinatingly, Millennium Capital Management Ltd. noted that it “has implemented additional LED lighting and passive infrared sensors in some London office locations.” It also noted that its employees are “the single most important element in determining the success of the business.”

item.title: Morning Coffee: Jane Street's big white men with sparse LinkedIn profiles. HSBC's awkward new trading floor
item.description:
Who runs Jane Street? </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-jane-street> Could it be Rob Granieri </news/rob-granieri-jane-street>, the hairy 53-year-old billionaire who goes to Burning Man? Could it be Turner Batty </news/jane-street-12bn-loss>, the curiously named man who addressed Jane Street employees when the firm lost $15bn in July? Could it be a group of 26 people, nine of whom are on the management committee and the rest of whom run things like US options or commodities trading?
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/features/2026-jane-street-guide-power-players/?taid=6abd7bd4aae84d0001b8789d&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>thinks Jane Street is run by a group and it has dug up their names. These we have listed in the table below. Achieving the names is a feat, because unlike other organisations, where people with big jobs boast of their corporate adventures on LinkedIn, Jane Street's people are ultra low key.
Most of Jane Street's low key leaders are men. Almost all are white men. One is a woman - Marie Harrison, who is a CFO of subsidiaries. Marie and others among Jane Street's elite have profiles on LinkedIn, but Marie's profile lists no more than her name and employer. Bloomberg notes that this is a Jane Street thing: when you join the firm, you pare everything back and are as cryptic as possible. You will not find Jane Street people declaring themselves "excited" about "surging momentum" or travelling the world to photograph themselves embracing disparate employees.
A cryptic LinkedIn profile has, in fact, always been the ultimate flex. TGS people don't even say where they work (until they move to Citadel </news/morning-coffee-what-it-s-like-when-citadel-really-wants-you-another-jp-morgan-expenses-case>). The world could maybe benefit from more of this. If you want to network with Granieri you probably need to find him at Burning Man.
Separately, HSBC may have dumped most of its M&A and ECM bankers </news/hscb-closure-europe-us-job-cuts>in Europe and the US, but it still likes traders and it even has a new trading floor in its new office at Panorama St. Paul's.
Unfortunately, though, the new trading floor does not sound very panoramic. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-01/hsbc-s-new-city-trading-floor-is-far-shorter-than-banking-rivals?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261001&utm_campaign=author_20887312>says it has unusually low ceilings of just 2.6m versus 3.75m for the trading floor at the old HSBC office in Canary Wharf. Goldman Sachs in London has 3.2m trading floor ceilings. UBS has 3.5m.
HSBC's traders may therefore feel a bit claustrophic. Not so, says HSBC, which declares: "We are very pleased with our upcoming move to Panorama St Paul’s in early 2027 and our headquarters will offer a newly redesigned, modern workspace including a remodeled, state-of-the-art trading floor right in the heart of the City of London.”
This could probably be added to LinkedIn.
Meanwhile...
Situational Awareness was allegedly asking for 10x leverage and had had been paying banks a larger-than-normal spread to incentivise them to help with this endeavour. (NY Times) <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/30/business/situational-awareness-stock-market-leverage.html>
Oura is delaying its IPO. So are Holtec Nuclear Corp and Bamboo Insurance Services Inc. Everyone is waiting for Anthropic. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-29/smart-ring-maker-oura-postpones-ipo-due-to-market-uncertainty?srnd=homepage-americas>
Lorna Hajdini renewed her countersuit against Chirayu Rana </news/chirayu-rana-jpmorgan>and says he fabricated his allegations to extract money from her and from JPMorgan. Chirayu Rana's lawyer says he stands by them. (NYPost) <https://nypost.com/2026/09/29/business/jpmorgan-chase-exec-accused-by-ex-banker-of-forcing-him-to-become-her-sex-slave-renews-countersuit-against-him/?dicbo=v2-LbAwqga>
If you want to work for SpaceX you'll need to be prepared for 60 hour weeks and "be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.” You must also have "kind of raw, innate intelligence,” and be ok with Elon Musk looking at your CV. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-30/what-it-takes-to-get-a-job-at-elon-musk-s-spacex?taid=6abd01f5c3ffd8000132991c&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
It might be a good time to work in infrastructure investment in Europe. The continent needs $800bn of infrastucture investment a year, says KKR. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-30/kkr-sees-europe-needing-800-billion-a-year-for-infrastructure?taid=6abd00c9c3ffd80001329901&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Barclays hired Tristan Wood, who was BNP Paribas' global head of FX options.
<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-29/jpmorgan-hires-three-for-natural-resources-banking-team> < https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-29/wells-fargo-hires-jpmorgan-s-david-harkin-to-co-lead-tech-deals> <https://www.ft.com/content/2a62022e-219b-4eb2-b5d7-c2bb01688acc?syn-25a6b1a6=1> <https://www.ft.com/content/3b5b46d7-2dcf-40f0-82f3-65ab6e4be76b?shareType=nongift&syn-25a6b1a6=1>& <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-29/mckinsey-partner-s-online-comments-on-female-leaders-spark-rebuke?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc5MDY5NDE3NiwiZXhwIjoxNzkxMjk4OTc2LCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUTTRSTjNSMjRVOEUwMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiIwRDk2NDEyNEIwMzE0OTI0QTBFNkY4OUUwODFCOEQwQyJ9.gs5809cMd-DYhh33EVwgxEkB6xN5QzaLVMLxmCo2yBo> <https://x.com/MadameButcher> <https://www.linkedin.com/in/sarahbutcherjournalist/> </about/editor-tips>

item.title: Citi's 2026 layoffs have been more frequent and widespread than we thought
item.description:
Citi is cutting costs and with them, jobs. As we reported earlier this month </news/citi-job-cuts-2026-new-york>, the bank has made three rounds of job cuts in New York so far this year, encompassing 820 people. But this appears to be just the tip of the iceberg.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Sources say that Citi has made additional layoffs this year, affecting its mostly middle and back office employees </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking> in places like Tampa, Florida, O'Fallon, Missouri or Florence, Kentucky. Some of those let go were at the bank for over two decades.
The most recent round of cuts is thought to have happened a few weeks ago, with many of those affected having their last days at the bank this week. Teams working on regulatory reporting, risk, compliance, KYC and fraud detection are thought to have been included in the cuts.
A spokesperson for Citi said: "We are grateful for the contributions these colleagues have made to Citi." She said "As we said previously, we will continue to reduce our headcount globally in 2026," and that the changes to headcount reflect adjustments to "staffing levels, locations and expertise" to "align with Citi's business needs, efficiencies we have gained through technology; and progress against our Transformation work, which is nearing Citi’s target state."
Some of the eliminated jobs have been automated. Some have moved offshore. Some have been subjected to both of these things. Citi has a "Solutions Center" in Costa Rica, for example, and is currently hiring project managers there to work on its "data governance foundation." Tim Ryan, the vigorous former PWC partner </news/kathryn-ruemmler-goldman-sachs>who's tasked with cleaning up Citi's data issues and thus escaping its 2020 consent order <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465920113933/tm2032793d1_ex99-3.htm>, was in Costa Rica a few weeks ago and said Citi employees there are using AI in "powerful, practical ways."
Citi is thought to have made rolling cuts across the US this year, not all of which have been documented in WARN notices due to varying documentation rules by state. More cuts are expected in the weeks to come.
In July, we noted </news/citi-has-quietly-cut-7-000-jobs-this-year-what-about-the-other-9-000>that Citi had cut 7,000 jobs in six months but that it still employed 9,000 more people than before the consent order was imposed. Citi hasn't said that it wants to reduce headcount back to its pre-consent order level. But CFO Gonzalo Luchetti <https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/investor-day/citi-ID26-financial-overview-presentation.pdf> has said that as transformation work relating to the order nears an end, costs will be trimmed. This is being combined with a "structural efficiency push" that has mapped over 100 processes for automation.
Citi insiders who have been let go after spending their entire careers at the bank said it's a "tough transition."
